newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Aleman says Ortega asks for meeting in Nicaragua.
newsitem.headline: Aleman says Ortega asks for meeting in Nicaragua.

text.p: Nicaraguan President Arnoldo Aleman on Sunday said he had received a letter from arch-rival Daniel Ortega of the Sandinista Front offering to meet, easing fears of political instability in Nicaragua.

"Yesterday, we received a letter from Comandante Ortega accepting the offer of dialogue we had proposed to lead this country to progress and development," Aleman, who took office on Friday, told reporters.
Aleman, the former mayor of the capital Managua, said he would answer Ortega's letter on Monday and would consider the 14 points for discussion Ortega mentioned in the note.
No date has been set for the meeting, he said.

Nicaragua remains bitterly polarised between the left-wing Sandinistas and Aleman's right-wing Liberal Alliance, and analysts have warned the two must sit down and reach an understanding if the country is to be governable.

The Sandinistas, who governed Nicaragua from 1979 to 1990 with Ortega at the helm, have a history of violent street protests and used their muscle to frustrate the government of former President Violeta Chamorro in its early days.
